v1.14.0 SHIPPED 2026-05-05 (tag 290ffe0). All five theme E issues closed: #99 (project-resolution refusal, PR #104, d9126b4), #102 (MCP audit absolute path, PRs #106/#107, 001ac9e), #100 + #101 (size-budget shed + write-amp guard, PR #108, d18923f), #103 (tier semantics docs, PR #109, 7e27140). Plus polish fix eab1c9b (pathological notice + tier describe alignment).

Release was clean: workflow first try landed all 4 artifacts (no #98 retry needed), Homebrew tap auto-updated to 1.14.0 (847a6a6 on seabearDEV/homebrew-ccli). Smoke-tested production binary end-to-end against CODEX_BOOTSTRAP_MAX_BYTES=500 — trimmed notice + pathological-overflow notice + tier:full bypass + #99 refusal all behave as designed.

Test count: 1325 (post-v1.13) → 1394 (+69 across the v1.14 cycle).

DOGFOODING PART THREE: still expected as the natural narrative sequel to v1.13's part two. Theme: "the loop closed and showed us a hole" + "we codified the soak policy from the same data" + "guardrails grew from the FA-iOS dataset mine". Not a release blocker, but the v1.14 cycle is the strongest case study yet.

v1.15 PREP: project.v115Hints already records the search-leverage signal from the user's v1.14 trim conversation. #84 (entry health) deferred from v1.14 — pairs naturally with the search theme. Soak-exit policy (project.soakPolicy) is N=1 calibration; v1.15 is the second sample.

NEXT SESSION LIKELY PICKS UP: dogfooding Part Three writing, OR v1.15 Phase 1 soak observation (open the data window now that v1.14 is in production), OR a triage of any post-release surprises that surface.
